record.original_question: Every polycyclic group can be embedded into GL(n, Z) for some n in N, and matrix representations can sometimes be computed from a polycyclic presentation. What is the computational complexity of finding a matrix representation of a polycyclic group?

evidence.quote: It is well-known that every polycyclic group can be embedded into GL(n, Z) for some n in N. For groups that are additionally torsion-free and nilpotent, a matrix representation can be computed.
(6) What is the complexity of finding matrix representation of polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series $G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_n = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $G_{i-1}/G_i$ is cyclic. Every polycyclic group can be specified by a polycyclic presentation, i.e. a finite presentation on generators $g_1,\dots,g_n$ encoding the cyclic factors of such a series together with conjugation and power relations. It is a classical result that every polycyclic group $G$ can be embedded as a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{Z})$ for some $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and various algorithms are known for computing such an embedding (in particular when $G$ is torsion-free and nilpotent).

Determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given a polycyclic presentation of a polycyclic group $G$, compute an integer $d$ and an explicit faithful representation $\rho : G \hookrightarrow \mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{Z})$, i.e. matrices $\rho(g_1),\dots,\rho(g_n) \in \mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{Z})$ generating an isomorphic copy of $G$. Specifically, establish tight upper and lower bounds, as a function of the input size, on the time complexity of producing such a matrix representation, and on the bit-size of the resulting matrices and dimension $d$.
artifact.status_search_result: Practical algorithms for constructing integer matrix representations of polycyclic groups exist (e.g., by Lo, Ostheimer, Assmann, Eick), and several have been implemented in computer algebra systems. However, no precise complexity bounds appear to have been established. The problem is listed as an open question on the SciLag problem repository for computational complexity in polycyclic groups, indicating it remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Practical Algorithm for Finding Matrix Representations for Polycyclic Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Practical algorithm for constructing an integer matrix representation of a polycyclic group from a polycyclic presentation.
status_evidence.claim: Practical (not complexity-analyzed) algorithms exist for the problem.

status_evidence.title: Computational Complexity of Group Theoretic Problems in Polycyclic Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem listing on computational complexity questions for polycyclic groups.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity questions for polycyclic groups remain listed as open problems.
